sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Roosendaal adopted a new parking plan in January 2026 that keeps parking possible but organises it more smartly. The council approved the Parkeerbeleidsplan on 29 January 2026, with better laid-out spaces, clearer garages and new mobility hubs, aiming to free street space for greenery and meeting [0]; the plan says fewer car spaces are needed in the centre and station area, where cycling and public transport links are good, and more in districts and villages, with measures phased [1]. At the committee stage on 8 January the alderman said it works in two phases, first fixing problem spots and then steering behaviour through differentiated tariffs, that he does not favour blue zones and that existing permits will not be taken away [2]. The council also adopted new parking standards for new developments on 29 January 2026, in force from 9 February 2026, with a 25 percent reduction near the station and buy-off sums of 5,000 to 15,000 euros per space [4][5].

On pricing, the council adopted the 2026 parking-tax ordinance on 18 December 2025, with street parking at 2.65 euros an hour in area A and 2.05 euros in area B and a 10-euro day ticket [6]. Residents in the paid area can get a permit for at most two plates [14]. A consultant's draft presentation of October 2025 said street parking pressure is high in the inner city and districts while the garages are often empty in the evening and at night [3].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Development is in studies. The Mobiliteitsvisie 2040 aims for a car-light inner city, a new western entrance to the Nieuwe Markt garage and a park-and-ride at Leisurepark Roosendaal [15], and the Mobiliteitsagenda 2025-2040 lists a 25,000-euro feasibility study for the western entrance, a parking hub study for Dunantstraat and a mobility hub at the station as planned work [16]. A 2025 order designates paid-only parking in the Dominestraat, the Kade, Molenstraat and part of Emile van Loonpark, and permit-only parking in Van Dregtplein and Dr. van Dregtstraat [8]. Vattenfall InCharge is placing public charge points through 2028, and the garages Nieuwe Markt, Biggelaar, Roselaar and Mill Hill have charging spaces [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Parkeer Beheer Roosendaal runs the five city-centre garages: Nieuwe Markt (520 spaces), Biggelaar (375), Roselaar (416), Mill Hill (100, plus 200 at weekends) and Liga (150, weekends only) [11]. Since 1 January 2025 all five charge 0.75 euro per 20 minutes with a 10-euro day ticket [9]. In November 2023 the municipality had planned a 5-cent rise per 20 minutes because the company needed about 310,000 euros more income [10]. Entry is by plate recognition, with contactless payment, and about 40 street machines accept only cashless payment [12]. A resident subscription for Nieuwe Markt costs 273.10 euros a quarter [13].

Our data cover seven car parks with 1,818 spaces, the five garages and two station park-and-rides, measured for about eight weeks since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 28% on weekdays, weighted by spaces, and rose at weekends in the big garages. Nieuwe Markt, the largest, averaged 32% on weekdays and 43% at weekends and reached full in a single Saturday-evening reading; Biggelaar rises from 20% to 42%. Roselaar (415) is the quietest large garage at 20% and 24%. This matches the consultant's remark that the garages are rarely full, though they fill on Saturday evenings. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
